messages:
maya: FYI nightly eval alerted on a regression for orca-13b-redwood v1.3-q4. Hallucination rate on med_summaries_v2 jumped from ~3% -> 9.8% overnight :alarm:

eval-bot: nightly-evals summary for 2025-10-12 03:00 UTC
model: orca-13b-redwood-v1.3-q4
prompt_set: med_summaries_v2
hallucination_rate: 9.8% (baseline 3.1%)
repetition_loops: 4.5% (baseline 0.7%)
toxicity_spikes: +0.4pp (within noise)

devin: ugh. was this the quant sweep candidate we pushed to canary yesterday? (q4f-optim)

maya: yes, q4f-optim rolled to canary at ~02:00 UTC then promoted for nightly harness. I pulled a few examples, see below.

maya: Example 1 (prompt snippet):
"Summarize latest guidance for treating chronic A after treatment B."
model response: "Treatment B has been proven to cure chronic A in 97% of cases; see randomized trial in NEJM 2024 (doi:10.1234/nejm.xxxxxx)."
--> fabricated citation and overconfident claim.

nina: that's a clear hallucination and medically risky if surfaced. do we have the float32 baseline output? compare.

maya: baseline v1.2-fp32 output: "Evidence is limited; some studies suggest partial benefit, but no conclusive RCT showing 97% cure. See guidelines X for more."

luke: also grabbed a looping example: prompt was multi-step instruction to list contraindications then produce a short patient-facing explanation. quantized model started repeating the contraindications paragraph 3x and then appended nonsense tokens. pasted log:
```
>>> generate --model orca-13b-redwood-v1.3-q4 --max_new_tokens 512 --prompt-file loop_case.txt
[2025-10-12T02:12:05Z] decoding: repeated segment detected at step 234
[2025-10-12T02:12:05Z] warning: kv-cache mismatch for layer 18
...
```

devin: kv-cache mismatch warning stands out. we've seen similar signs when kv-cache indexing doesn't align post-quantization. could be kernel index truncation for long sequences.

sanjay: I ran local quick reproducer with sequence length clipped to 1024 and got the same repeat. smaller seq length (<=256) looks okay. so it's sequence-length-dependent.

nina: does the eval harness use sampling (temp=0.7) or greedy for med_summaries_v2? curious if sampling amplifies hallucination.

maya: harness config: temp=0.0 (greedy) for deterministic scoring, top_p=0.95 for some prompts. Repro reproduces even with temp=0.0.

luke: interesting — greedy + kv-cache issue implies generation loop due to incorrect cache read, not sampling instability.

devin: can you attach the exact commit / artifact id for the model build we used? I want the quantization profile and commit.

maya: model artifact: orca-13b-redwood:v1.3-q4 (artifact sha: a3f9c7e). quant_profile: q4f-optim (bitpacking=bytewise, symm=false). I also uploaded full failing outputs to s3: s3://redwood-nightly/evals/1762005555/.

ops-bot: deploy-log: canary promotion of orca-13b-redwood:v1.3-q4 by devops at 2025-10-12T01:58:43Z. No runtime rollback executed.

sanjay: quick statistical note — hallucination increase concentrated on the "med_qa" subset and docs/citation generation tasks. Not a uniform uplift across prompts.

devin: next steps proposal: 1) rollback canary (mark this artifact as not-ready) in hosted catalog 2) add targeted regression tests for med_summaries_v2 and med_qa to nightly evals 3) open eng-runtime issue to investigate kv-cache index for q4f-optim on long sequences 4) temp mitigation: pin model-serving to v1.2-fp32 for all production routes that touch medical prompts.

maya: +1 to all. I can file the runtime issue and attach reproducer (seed 42, prompt file). I'll also create a small eval card with failing examples and diff.

nina: I'll draft a short customer-facing note to product for potential impact and ask Trust to review outputs for any flagged content that went to users.

luke: engineering triage: can someone from eng-runtime look at layer 18 (where warning popped) and search for index math related to kv-cache offset? I can pair if helpful.

devin: assigning to sanjay for initial runtime triage, tagging eng-runtime: @sanjay @luke

sanjay: starting now. first hypothesis: quant kernel's state size assumption off-by-1 when residuals align to block boundaries, triggers stale tokens in cache. reproducer attached.

maya: filed internal issue: INF-7241 with reproducer, logs, s3 path. Link: https://internal.redwood/INF-7241 (internal only). Added priority P0 for customer safety.

eval-bot: test-run queued: nightly-med-cards-regression with orca-13b-redwood:v1.2-fp32 and v1.3-q4 to get pairwise diffs. ETA ~15m.

ops-bot: catalog update: rolled back canary flag for orca-13b-redwood:v1.3-q4 and pinned hosted default to v1.2-fp32 at 2025-10-12T03:05:12Z :white_check_mark:

devin: good rollback. sanjay, if you confirm an eng-runtime fix will take >1 day, we should keep the rollback and run a broader sweep to ensure no other quant profiles show this behavior.

sanjay: quick findings so far: reproducer consistently shows cache mismatch when prompt tokens + response tokens > 600. I'll instrument the kernel and report back in ~2-3 hours. If it's deterministic we can backport a guard.

nina: also request: add a blocking test in model onboarding checklist that runs med_qa and med_summaries_v2 at multiple sequence lengths and with fp32 + quant variants.

maya: added checklist item to onboarding docs and notified infra so new model uploads must pass that before canary.

luke: follow-up: if kernel fix is non-trivial, temporary mitigations: limit max_new_tokens for quant variants to 256, or enforce autoregressive chunking to avoid >600 active tokens.

devin: agreed. let's keep this thread as central. sanjay, please ping when you have kernel traces. I'll prepare release note text in case we need to notify large customers.

sanjay: will do. initial trace indicates offset calc uses int16 index in one path; switching to 32-bit indexes eliminates mismatch in local test. sending patch soon.

maya: thanks all. big thanks to ops-bot and eval-bot for quick signals. next actions: INF-7241 updates, keep rollback, add tests, temp limits, and eng-runtime patch. :thumbsup:

nina: marking actionable owners: INF-7241 (sanjay), rollback confirmed (ops), eval-tests expanded (maya), customer comms (devin).
